messages:
Sam R: Quick thread 11: we need a clear migration story for rollout metadata schema changes. Additive proto fields are fine but clients parse strings today; how do we version intent so runtime doesn't misinterpret unknown fields as safe?

Priya S: Agree. Suggest we publish a small `schema_version` field (string) in rollout metadata and a `compatibility_level` enum: backward_compatible|additive_only|breaking. Default to additive_only for now. Runtime uses compatibility_level to alter eviction/promote heuristics.

Maya C: +1 but ops question: authors might forget to set compatibility_level. Can we make the build-pipeline annotate the value automatically based on diff heuristics (e.g., tokenizer or config changed => breaking)? Then release author can override.

Ben O: That seems doable. Build pipeline can compute a fingerprint diff and heuristics to infer compatibility, then insert inferred_compatibility and author_override fields. We should also emit a required `change_label` short string so Console shows human intent.

schema-bot: Deploy note: adding fields schema_version, compatibility_level, inferred_compatibility, author_override, change_label to rollout proto in staging. All fields are optional/strings to maintain backwards compat.

Sam R: Runtime semantics proposal: if compatibility_level==breaking or inferred_compatibility==breaking and author_override!="allow", then evict immediately and emit alert. If additive_only or backward_compatible, apply soft-promotion windows. If schema_version mismatch (runtime < metadata.schema_version), treat as unknown -> default to conservative path (treat as breaking unless inference says otherwise).

Priya S: We should also add a `client_contract` field that enumerates which client surfaces changed (tokenizer, input_schema, output_schema, logits_shape). That helps runtime decide whether to route or to force strict tenant policies. Eg: client_contract:["tokenizer","output_schema"].

Maya C: Nice. Also we need a clear mapping for tenant overrides: tenant profiles can clamp max compatibility_level they accept. E.g., enterprise_tenant may set max_allowed=backward_compatible only. We'll document precedence: explicit author_override -> tenant_policy clamp -> runtime default.

Ben O: Telemetry: emit events `rollout_schema_inferred`, `rollout_schema_override`, and `rollout_schema_mismatch_reclaim`. Include fingerprints and change_label in events so Console can correlate. Also write a short deprecation doc for older clients that ignore new fields: if runtime sees unknown schema_version and can't safely infer, it should not auto-promote to hot.

Sam R: Action items: Priya -> update build-pipeline to compute inferred_compatibility and client_contract heuristics; Maya -> draft RFC text for schema_version and precedence rules; Ben -> add telemetry events and Console rendering for change_label; Ops -> ensure reclaim/pressure still overrides soft promotions.

Priya S: One more: include a tiny `migration_notes` freeform string where authors can put migration steps for clients (e.g., "clients must use new tokenizer v2 or expect token offsets to change"). Console surfaces prominently for tenants.

Sam R: Great. TL;DR: add schema_version + compatibility_level + inferred_compatibility + client_contract + migration_notes + change_label; default conservative behavior on unknown versions; build-pipeline auto-infers and authors can override; tenant policies clamp.
